This change makes `getBoxesAlongSlice` actually filter boxes. The modified condition is correct and doesn't drop any box the slice needs.

**The old code kept every box.** With `min <= max`, `(par_index >= min) || (par_index <= max)` is always true. So every refinement box in the domain was sent to `refineElements`, wherever it sat relative to the slice.

**The new filter never drops a needed box.**
- Box corners from `getBoxesInLevelIndex` are unique-knot indices at the box's level. `findElementIndex(par)` on `m_bases[l]` returns an index of the same kind, so the comparison is consistent.

I found no runtime defect in the new cycle-breaking code. I traced it against how the polylines are actually produced (`gsHDomain::getPolylines` → `gsAAPolyline::writeParasolidUnsigned` → `gsHTensorBasis::domainBoundariesGeneric`).

- **Polyline format:** each polyline is a closed sequence of segments, where each segment shares an end with the next one, and the last connects back to the first. Each segment is stored lowest point first (`x1<=x2`, `y1<=y2`). There are no zero-length segments, and collinear vertical pieces are already merged.
- **`identifyCycle`:** for each segment it correctly finds the point it shares with the next segment, by checking which end of segment k lies on segment k+1. A point visited twice is a "kissing" corner, and `index[P]` correctly records the segment that starts at that point. In a grid of axis-aligned lines at most four segments meet at a point, so the `times > 2` throw can only fire on malformed input.
- **`breakPolylineIntoTwoParts`:** starting at that segment, only four segments touch P: the two at the first visit and the two at the second. So the first part runs to the segment that closes the first loop, and the second part takes the rest, including both wrap-around segments. Neither part can be empty. I ran two cases by hand: two squares touching at a corner, and a hole touching the outer boundary at a corner. Both split into the correct pair of loops.
- **No crossing loops:** the boundary walk keeps the region on the same side, so after a split each loop still turns at P. The two loops touch at P but never cross.
- **Bounding boxes:** `findNewAABB` builds the boxes from the same unique-knot array of `maxLevel()` (`m_tree.getMaxInsLevel()`) that `domainBoundariesGeneric` used to turn indices into parameters. The values match exactly, so the new boxes use the same index space as the old ones. Taking the min of the first-point coordinates and the max of the second-point coordinates is correct for the stored segment order.
- **Hole/boundary classification:** a pinch point always lies strictly inside the box of its own region. So a hole or island that touches its container only at that point still has a box strictly inside the container's box. The existing parity test and nearest-containing-box assignment in `decomposeDomain` therefore classify the split loops correctly.
- **`breakCycles` loop:** `aabb` and `polylines` grow in step. `line--` on a `size_t` at 0 wraps and is then incremented back to 0, which is well-defined. Each split removes at least one double visit, so the loop always terminates.

Two things are not blockers under the runtime-only criterion:
1. `if (!p1 and !p2)` is the only use of `and` as an operator in the codebase. It is standard C++ and compiles on GCC/Clang. But MSVC (which the project supports, see `gsConfig.cmake` and `CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST`) rejects it without `/permissive-` or `/Za`. That would break the MSVC build of `gsTHBSpline_.cpp`, so `&&` would be safer.
2. Judging nesting by bounding boxes can still misclassify a separate region that sits in the notch of a non-convex region. That problem existed before this change.

votes.reasoning:
This change breaks the existing conforming (non-dG) IETI path in debug builds.

**The defect**
- `computeJumpMatrices` now always calls `helper()` (`gsIetiMapper.hpp:347`). It is not limited to mappers with artificial dofs (`m_status&2`).
- The first loop in `helper()` (lines 452–466) goes over the real dofs of every patch and checks `GISMO_ASSERT( dofs(globalIndex,0) == 0, "Internal error.")`. That only holds if each free global dof belongs to exactly one patch. It is true for the dG mapper built by `gsArtificialIfaces`, which asserts `coupledSize()==0` on the original mapper. It is false for conforming mappers:
  - `ieti_example` calls `u.setup(bc, dirichlet::interpolation, 0)`, which runs `matchInterface` on every interface.
  - `ieti2_example` uses `iFace::glue`.
  - In both, dofs on a shared interface have the same global index on several patches.
- The value 0 means both "not set yet" and "patch 0", so the check only passes when the earlier patch was patch 0. Take three patches in a row, P0 | P1 | P2: at k=1 the P1/P2 interface dofs are written as `dofs(gi,0)=1`, and at k=2 the assertion fails.
- `GISMO_ASSERT` throws `std::logic_error` in any build without `NDEBUG` (`gsDebug.h:89-92`). The default `yeti_mp2.xml` has 21 patches, 84 after the default split, so this fails on the first run. Even the four sub-patches of patch 0 hit it, for example at their shared centre corner.
- Every example is registered as a CTest test (`add_test` in `cmake/gismoUse.cmake`). So `ieti_example` and `ieti2_example`, and any user code doing conforming IETI, now throw inside `computeJumpMatrices` in Debug builds. Before this commit they worked.

**Release builds and performance**
In release builds the assertion is compiled out. The first loop then just overwrites entries, and there are no artificial dofs, so `helper()` does nothing useful. It still allocates a `freeSize()×2` index matrix and scans every dof on every call, which is small but wasted work. The removed `preImage` loop in `cornersAsPrimals` was O(N) per corner, so taking it out is a performance gain, not a regression. I found no real performance regression; the reason to reject is the debug-build failure above.

**Lesser concern**
`helper()` only copies primal constraints that already exist when it runs. `ieti2_example`, which this commit doesn't touch, still calls `computeJumpMatrices` before `cornersAsPrimals`. That is harmless for conforming mappers, but dG callers who use that order will silently get no copied constraints.

**Suggested fix**
Only call `helper()` when `m_status&2` is set. Alternatively, start `dofs` at -1 with `setConstant(-1)` instead of 0 and only check for single ownership in the artificial-dof case.
